1- Import the required libraries
```{r}
#Call the libraries
library(tidyverse)
library(WGCNA)
library(ggplot2)
```


2- Import you data. Here I use a sample data (random) to be used as an example.
Note: The data could be heavy for you system. In case, remove some of the rows and a few of the samples.
```{r}
df <- read.csv("log2_cpm_matrix_test.csv", check.names = FALSE)
rownames(df) <- df[,1]
df <- df[,-1]
df_expression <- df[-1,]
```



---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
3- prepare data for WGCNA
*Get the gene expression as "datExpr0" 
*Check if the quality of genes are OK using "goodSamplesGenes"
Note: There are multiple steps to remove low quality genes. check the literature. 
Note: The data could be used as Log2(transcriptome) or Log10(lipidome and other statistical analysis) transformed.
Note: Avoid using a list of differentially expressed genes.

```{r prepare data for WGCNA}
options(stringsAsFactors = FALSE) #Make sure to do this

datExpr0 <- as.data.frame(t(df_expression))
datExpr1 <- as.data.frame(lapply(datExpr0, as.numeric))
rownames(datExpr1) <- rownames(datExpr0)

#To check quality of data
gsg = goodSamplesGenes(datExpr1, verbose = 3, )
gsg$allOK

#If gsg$allOK returns FALSE follow this code to remove bad genes.
datExpr1_clean <- datExpr1[gsg$goodSamples, gsg$goodGenes]

gsg_clean <- goodSamplesGenes(datExpr1_clean, verbose = 3)
gsg_clean$allOK
```

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
4- Cluster the samples and see if there is any outlier
```{r, fig.width=8, fig.height=8}
sampleTree = hclust(dist(datExpr1_clean), method = "average")

sizeGrWindow(8,8)
{plot(sampleTree, main = "Sample clustering to detect outliers", sub="",
     xlab="", #To remove x axis label
     cex.main = 1,#Main title
     cex.axis = 0.5,#Axis label
     cex.lab = 1,#Axis label
     cex = 0.4,
     )

abline(h = 12, col = "red")} #Only can be used in the consule mode.
```

If you want to remove outlier clusters use the follwoing code.
Note: Here we do not use it. Consider using it in your work. In case of applying use "datExpr_no_outlier"
for the next steps of the analysis.

```{r}
clust = cutreeStatic(sampleTree, cutHeight = 15, minSize = 10)
table(clust)

keepSamples = (clust==1)
datExpr_no_outlier = datExpr1_clean[keepSamples, ]
```

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
5-Prepare the traits
Note: the traits should be numerical, 0 and 1 for absence and presence of the trait. 
For example, if sample is male it is 1 for male and 0 for female columns. 
For continues numerical (weight and height) keep it as numerical to find the 
association between changes in the data and the trait.

```{r}
Data_treat <- data.frame(cell_type = t(df[1,]))

traitData <- data.frame(Cell_sample = rownames(Data_treat),
                        Stem_cells = ifelse(Data_treat$cell_type == "Stem_cells",1,0),
                        B_cells = ifelse(Data_treat$cell_type == "B_cells",1,0),
                        T_cells = ifelse(Data_treat$cell_type == "T_cells",1,0)
                        )
head(traitData)
```

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
6- Combine the matrix of values with the traits dataframe to see the 
distribution of traits based on the clustering of samples.
Note: To get any export from the plots use "pdf()" or "png()" functions.

```{r}
Samples = rownames(datExpr1_clean)
traitRows = match(Samples, traitData$Cell_sample)
datTraits = traitData[traitRows, -1]
rownames(datTraits) = traitData[traitRows, 1]
collectGarbage()

sampleTree2 = hclust(dist(datExpr1_clean), method = "average",)
traitColors = numbers2colors(datTraits, signed = FALSE, colors = c("white","skyblue"))
sizeGrWindow(12,8)
par(cex = 0.5)
plotDendroAndColors(sampleTree2, traitColors,
                    groupLabels = names(datTraits),
                    main = "Sample dendrogram and trait heatmap", cex.dendroLabels = 0.4, 
                    cex.colorLabels = 0.6, addGuide = FALSE, guideAll = FALSE, setLayout = TRUE, 
                    colorHeight = 0.1, autoColorHeight = TRUE, colorHeightBase = 0.2, 
                    colorHeightMax = 0.3,)
```

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
7- Calculating soft power for the analysis. 

```{r}
powers = c(c(1:10), seq(from = 12, to=20, by=2))
sft = pickSoftThreshold(datExpr0, powerVector = powers, verbose = 5, )
```

*Plot the results
```{r}
sizeGrWindow(9, 5)
par(mfrow = c(1,2))
cex1 = 0.9

{plot(sft$fitIndices[,1], -sign(sft$fitIndices[,3])*sft$fitIndices[,2],
     xlab="Soft Threshold (power)",ylab="Scale Free Topology Model Fit,signed R^2",type="n",
     main = paste("Scale independence"))
text(sft$fitIndices[,1], -sign(sft$fitIndices[,3])*sft$fitIndices[,2],
     labels=powers,cex=cex1,col="red")


abline(h=0.8,col="red")}

```

```{r}
sizeGrWindow(9, 5)
par(mfrow = c(1,2))
cex1 = 0.9

{plot(sft$fitIndices[,1], sft$fitIndices[,5],
     xlab="Soft Threshold (power)",ylab="Mean Connectivity", type="n",
     main = paste("Mean connectivity"))
text(sft$fitIndices[,1], sft$fitIndices[,5], labels=powers, cex=cex1,col="red")}
```

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
8- Calculate adjacency, TOM, and dissTOM, select the best softPower based on the previous step. 
Usually the best softPower is the smallest value with R2 (y axis) above 0.8.
Try a couple to find he best clustering. Using different softPower usually won't make that much difference at the end.
NOTE: A random data has been used here. It may a few minutes to a few hours depending on your computer system and your dataset.
```{r}
softPower = 10
adjacency = adjacency(datExpr1_clean, power = softPower, type = "signed")

TOM = TOMsimilarity(adjacency)
dissTOM = 1-TOM

```

* Plot the resulting clustering tree using hierarchical clustering
```{r}
geneTree = hclust(as.dist(dissTOM), method = "average")
sizeGrWindow(12,9)
plot(geneTree, xlab="", sub="", main = "Gene clustering on TOM-based dissimilarity",
     labels = FALSE, hang = 0.04,)
```

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
9- Prepare the modules
```{r}
# We like large modules, so we set the minimum module size relatively high:
minModuleSize = 50
# Module identification using dynamic tree cut. change the threshold according to your data.
dynamicMods = cutreeDynamic(dendro = geneTree, distM = dissTOM, 
                            deepSplit = 3, pamRespectsDendro = FALSE,
                            minClusterSize = minModuleSize, method = "hybrid")
table(dynamicMods)
```

*To rename the modules from Color to something numerical (Optional!!! check the original code if you do not like this step and you need coloring)
```{r}
Module_number <- paste("M", c(1:45), sep = "") #Number of clusters from previous step
Module_in_number <- labels2colors(dynamicMods, colorSeq = Module_number)
table(Module_in_number)
```
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
10 - Combine the modules with similarities according to the mergeCloseModules().
```{r}
MEList = moduleEigengenes(datExpr1_clean, colors = Module_in_number,excludeGrey = TRUE,)
MEs = MEList$eigengenes

# Calculate dissimilarity of module eigengenes
MEDiss = 1-cor(MEs);
# Cluster module eigengenes
METree = hclust(as.dist(MEDiss), method = "average");
# Plot the result\
plot(METree, main = "Clustering of module eigengenes",
     xlab = "", sub = "")

#change according to your needs
MEDissThres = 0.2
abline(h=MEDissThres, col = "red")
#Merging
merge = mergeCloseModules(datExpr1_clean, Module_in_number, cutHeight = MEDissThres, verbose = 3)

mergedColors = merge$colors
mergedMEs = merge$newMEs

# Rename to moduleColors
moduleColors = mergedColors
# Construct numerical labels corresponding to the colors
colorOrder = c("grey", standardColors(50))
MEs = mergedMEs
```

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
11- Make the heatmap based on previous step
```{r}
nGenes = ncol(datExpr1_clean)
nSamples = nrow(datExpr1_clean)
# Recalculate MEs with color labels
MEs0 = moduleEigengenes(datExpr1_clean, moduleColors,)$eigengenes
MEs = orderMEs(MEs0)


moduleTraitCor = WGCNA::cor(MEs, datTraits, use = "pairwise.complete.obs", method = "spearman");

moduleTraitPvalue = corPvalueStudent(moduleTraitCor, nSamples)

textMatrix = paste(signif(moduleTraitCor, 2), "\n(",
                   signif(moduleTraitPvalue, 1), ")", sep = "");
dim(textMatrix) = dim(moduleTraitCor)

# Make the heatmap
color <- hcl.colors(100, palette = "PiYG")
par(mar = c(6, 8.5, 3, 3))

labeledHeatmap(Matrix = moduleTraitCor,
               xLabels = names(datTraits),
               yLabels = names(MEs),
               ySymbols = names(MEs),
               colorLabels = FALSE,
               colors = color,
               textMatrix = textMatrix,
               setStdMargins = FALSE,
               cex.text = 0.5,
               zlim = c(-1,1),
               main = paste("Module-trait relationships       "),cex.lab.x = 0.8,
               cex.lab.y = 0.8, legendLabel = "correlation", cex.legendLabel = 0.8)
```


---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
12- Define variable weight containing the weight column of datTrait.
```{r}
sample_type = as.data.frame(datTraits$Stem_cells);
names(sample_type) = "Stem_cells"

modNames = substring(names(MEs), 3)
geneModuleMembership = as.data.frame(cor(datExpr1_clean, MEs, use = "p"));
MMPvalue = as.data.frame(corPvalueStudent(as.matrix(geneModuleMembership), nSamples));
names(geneModuleMembership) = paste("MM", modNames, sep="");
names(MMPvalue) = paste("p.MM", modNames, sep="");
geneTraitSignificance = as.data.frame(cor(datExpr1_clean, sample_type, use = "p"));
GSPvalue = as.data.frame(corPvalueStudent(as.matrix(geneTraitSignificance), nSamples));
names(geneTraitSignificance) = paste("GS.", names(sample_type), sep="");
names(GSPvalue) = paste("p.GS.", names(sample_type), sep="");

#Note: If the gene names start with numbers it will return errors. Make sure it always starts with words.
annot <- data.frame(gene_annotation = colnames(datExpr1_clean)) #If you have external anootation use yours
probes = colnames(datExpr1_clean)
probes2annot = match(probes, annot$gene_annotation)
sum(is.na(probes2annot))

# Create the starting data frame
geneInfo0 = data.frame(Gene = probes,
                       geneSymbol = annot$gene_annotation[probes2annot],
                       moduleColor = moduleColors,
                       geneTraitSignificance,
                       GSPvalue)

# Order modules by their significance for weight
modOrder = order(-abs(cor(MEs, sample_type, use = "p")));
for (mod in 1:ncol(geneModuleMembership)){
  oldNames = names(geneInfo0)
  geneInfo0 = data.frame(geneInfo0, geneModuleMembership[, modOrder[mod]],
                         MMPvalue[, modOrder[mod]]);
  names(geneInfo0) = c(oldNames, paste("MM.", modNames[modOrder[mod]], sep=""),
                       paste("p.MM.", modNames[modOrder[mod]], sep=""))
}
# Order the genes in the geneInfo. 
geneOrder = order(geneInfo0$moduleColor, -abs(geneInfo0$GS.Stem_cells))# Change when you need other variables
geneInfo = geneInfo0[geneOrder, ]

table(geneInfo$moduleColor)

#Export the geneInfo as CSV file to use for other analyses (Gene Ontology, visualizing, ...).
write.csv(geneInfo, "geneInfo_stem_cells.csv")
```


---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
13- To have more control on the plot and make more advanced plots you can use ggplot.
```{r}
library(ggpubr)
geneInfo_M15 <- subset(geneInfo, geneInfo$moduleColor == "M10")

par(mar = c(6, 8.5, 3, 3))
ggplot(geneInfo_M15, aes(x = GS.Stem_cells, y = MM.M15)) +
  geom_point() +                                      # Scatter points
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, color = "blue") +
  stat_cor(method = "pearson", 
           size = 5)+
  theme(panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = "black", size = 0.2),
          plot.margin = margin(t = 20, r = 5, b = 5, l = 5),
          panel.border = element_rect(linetype = "solid", 
                                      size = 0.1, colour = "black", fill = NA),
          panel.grid.major.x = element_line(colour = "grey90", size = 0.1,),
          panel.grid.major.y = element_line(colour = "grey90", size = 0.1,),
          panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
          axis.text.x = element_text(size = 8, colour = "black"),
          axis.text.y = element_text(size = 8, colour = "black"))
  
```



---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
14- Export the network to visualize by Cytoscape software.
Note: exportNetworkToCytoscape(), exports two .TXT files (nodes, edges) to be used in Cytoscape.
```{r}
modules = "M10";
probes = names(datExpr1_clean)
inModule = is.finite(match(moduleColors, modules));
modProbes = probes[inModule];
modGenes = annot$gene_annotation[match(modProbes, annot$gene_annotation)];
modTOM = TOM[inModule, inModule]
dimnames(modTOM) = list(modProbes, modProbes)
cyt = exportNetworkToCytoscape(modTOM,
                               edgeFile = paste("CytoscapeInput-edges-", paste(modules, collapse="-"), ".txt", sep=""),
                               nodeFile = paste("CytoscapeInput-nodes-", paste(modules, collapse="-"), ".txt", sep=""),
                               weighted = TRUE,
                               threshold = 0.3, # Change based on what you need
                               nodeNames = modProbes,
                               altNodeNames = modGenes,
                               nodeAttr = moduleColors[inModule])

```


Note: There are other functions in WGCNA package. For more information chacke the package.
